text:
We checked “Packaging_Bad Folder” and found 9 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 3 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Threaded (linked) text frames
Frontify doesn’t support text flowing from one frame into another.
Where: the text frame “monobrand.comCrafted in Switzerl…” (page 1)
• Turn on View > Extras > Show Text Threads, then double-click a frame’s out port to break the thread so each frame holds its own text.
Learn more

2. Adobe Font missing from the package
Frontify only uses fonts included in the package; it can’t load Adobe Fonts from your Adobe account.
Where: the font “Playfair Display”
• Package again with File > Package and "Copy Fonts" checked, and check that the font’s files are in "Document fonts".
• If InDesign won’t copy the Adobe Font, use a licensed desktop copy of the font (or another font) instead.
Learn more

3. Embedded image
Frontify needs images as separate linked files and can’t read images embedded in the document.
Where: the image “monobrand-text-logo-black.png” (page 1)
• In Window > Links, select the image and choose Unembed Link from the panel menu.
• Save it into the Links folder and package again.
Learn more

4. Items on a master page
Frontify only reads items on the document pages, so anything on a master page (called a parent page in newer InDesign versions) is ignored or breaks the template.
Found on the master page: 1 rectangle
• In the Pages panel, open the master (parent) page and move its items onto the document pages, or delete them.
Learn more

5. Pasted graphic
Graphics pasted straight into InDesign aren’t linked files, so Frontify can’t read them.
• Save the graphic as a file (for example SVG, PDF or PNG), delete the pasted version and place the file with File > Place.
Learn more

6. Text aligned to the baseline grid
Frontify doesn’t use InDesign’s baseline grid, so line spacing will change.
Where: the paragraph style “Paragraph Style 2”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Indents and Spacing and set Align to Grid to None.
Learn more

7. Text frame has no paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: the text frame “monobrand.com” (page 1)
• Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

8. Unsupported font format
Frontify can only use OpenType (.otf) and TrueType (.ttf) fonts.
Where: the font “Futura.ttc”
• Get an OTF or TTF version from the font vendor and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.
Learn more

9. Variable font used
Frontify doesn’t support variable fonts, so text using them won’t render correctly.
Where: the font “Montserrat”
• Install the static (non-variable) version of the font and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.
Learn more

May change how it looks

10. Image frame is rotated
Rotation works, but the frame may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
Where: the image “monobrand-main-logo-black.png” (page 1, rotated 90°)
• Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, remove the rotation from the frame.
Learn more

11. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: the paragraph style “[Basic Paragraph]”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
Learn more

12. Text formatted outside its paragraph style
Formatting added by hand on top of a paragraph style (shown as a + next to the style name) may be lost or look different in Frontify.
Where: the text frame “monobrand.com” (page 1, font changed)
• Click into the text. A + after the style name in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles means it has extra formatting.
• To remove it, select the text and click Clear Overrides at the bottom of the Paragraph Styles panel.
• To keep the look, update the style to match instead (right-click the style > Redefine Style), or use a character style for single words.
Learn more

Worth a quick check (often fine as is)

13. Empty text frame
Empty frames are allowed, but are often left over by accident.
Where: a text frame on page 1
• Delete the frame if it isn’t needed.
Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
